newsitem.title: USA: Marriott International to sell 29 senior communities. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Marriott International to sell 29 senior communities. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]

text.p: A Marriott International Inc. subsidiary has agreed in principle to sell 29 of its senior living communities to Host Marriott Corp. in a deal valued at about $433 million (corrects from $540 million), the companies said Tuesday.
The acquisition will make Host Marriott one of the five largest owners of real estate used for senior living communities.
Under the agreement Marriott Senior Living Services will sell all of the common stock of Forum Group Inc., which owns the communities, to Host Marriott.
Marriott Senior Living Services will continue to operate the communities under the Marriott brand name.

Host Marriott will pay about $433 million for the existing communities and has set up a $107 million plan to add 1,075 living units by January 1999. About $44 million worth of new units are expected to be completed prior to closing in the second quarter.

The 29 communities are located in 11 states and, at closing, will include about 6,500 living units. After closing, Marriott said it expects to add about 700 suites or nursing care beds at certain communities.
Host Marriott, based in Bethesda, Md., said separately it expects the acquisition to generate about $55.2 million of earnings before interest, taxes and other items this year.

Host Marriott, which owns Marriott and Ritz-Carlton hotels, said the deal will bring the aggregate value of its 1997 acquisitions to over $800 million, or 80 percent of the company's goal of $1 billion for the year.
The sale is subject to approval of the companies' boards of directors and regulators and certain other conditions.

"The sale of these Marriott senior living communities is consistent with our strategy to grow through developing and operating strong hospitality businesses, while limiting our real estate holdings," said Michael Stein, executive vice president of Marriott International, based in Washington.
Forum Group communities offer independent and assisted living, Alzheimer's and nursing care units and have a 95 percent occupancy rate.

Over the next decade, it is estimated that the number of Americans age 85 and older will increase by more than 40 percent, while those age 75 and older will grow by over 25 percent, Host Marriot said.
Marriott International operates and franchises hotels under the Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, Courtyard, Fairfield Inns and Suites, Residence Inn, TownePlace Suites, and Executive Residences brands.
Host Marriott owns or holds controlling interests in 83 upscale and luxury full service hotel properties operated primarily under the Marriott and Ritz-Carlton brand names.
